r: Legitimacy by caliphal investiture: **mansur / khillat** from the Abbasid Caliph of **Baghdad (1229)**; Sultanate became part of **Dar-ul-Islam**; title **Sultan-i-Azam**; introduced the iqtadari system

**First** Muslim ruler with a theory like the **divine right of kings**: Sultan = **Niyabat-i-Khudai** (deputy of God), **Zil-i-Ilahi / Zillillah** (Shadow of God), next to the Paigambar; **sijda** and **paibos**; **blood and iron**; no low-born men in office; broke the Chahalgani; quelled Bengal
State interest above the ulema; "kingship knows no kinship"; **ignored the Caliph's authority** – sought no investiture, took **Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin** on his own
Rationalist absolutism; coin legend "**Al Sultan Zilli Allah**"; later sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in **Egypt**
Called himself "**Helper of a Caliph**" in his inscription on the **Garhmukteshwar** mosque
Silver coins in **Arabic and Devanagari Sanskrit**

0.x: The Sultans saw themselves as **representatives (lieutenants) of the Caliph**, naming him in the khutba and on coins – a nominal link; the Caliph had only moral authority.

r: **Religious affairs**, grants to mosques and madrasas
Most powerful post after the Sultan; controlled all departments in practice; the **Wazir** came next
Persian-Abbasid model; **heyday under the Tughlaqs** (Firoz's wazir **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul**)

1.x: **Deccan:** the Delhi model passed to the Bahmanis and **Qutb Shahis** – **Mir Jumla = finance**, Ain-ul-Mulk = army.
**Mir Bakshi** was a **Mughal** office – it did not exist under the Khaljis.

r: "The Forty" (Chalisa), created by **Iltutmish** – Turkish slave-nobles who made and unmade Sultans after him
Himself one of the Forty; **finally broke their power**
Nobles set aside his nominee **Kai Khusrau** and raised **Kaiqubad**
**Jalaluddin Khalji** seized power in **1290** – high office opened to **non-Turks and Indian Muslims**
Afghan tribal nobility; Sultan = **first among equals**
Ariz, freed from the Wazir's financial control
A **composite** government: **Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian** elements
Title Sultan, nominal Caliph, sijda, paibos, Nauroz
Army in **decimal units** with mounted archers
**State laws** (royal regulations) that supplemented the sharia
**Sharia** for Muslims (qazis); Hindus kept their personal laws (panchayats)
No fixed rule (no primogeniture) – acceptance by **nobles and ulema**, or **military strength**; Iltutmish nominated his daughter
Supreme military, legal and political authority; **commander-in-chief** and **final court of appeal**
